about: Machine-readable work queues for the six workstreams. GitHub Issues hold each story; this file says which story each workstream is on, what comes next and what blocks it. The orchestrator thread updates it at the weekly review and when a lead reports a story done. Check and render with: python docs/product/operations/tools/queues.py all

rules.needs_chris: New user-facing features need a mockup and Chris's typed go; Fabric capacity or cloud spend needs his typed yes. Such stories are blocked, never ready, until he answers.

WR-247.problem: tsql_errors.py maps 207, 208, 209, 239 and 8134 with certainty; arithmetic overflow and conversion errors still come out without a number.
acceptance: Arithmetic overflow and conversion failures show SQL Server's number and severity where certain, as WR-234 does for others
A test per mapped number; uncertain ones keep the plain message

WR-316.title: Unity Catalog names in Databricks SQL cells on this PC
WR-316.problem: Databricks notebooks name tables as catalog.schema.table; on this PC those names should resolve or be refused by name.
acceptance: main.default.t, USE CATALOG and USE SCHEMA and current_schema() answer as Databricks documents or are refused by name

WR-318.title: Snowflake: value-check the 16 Not checked functions against Snowflake's reference, or refuse them by name
WR-318.problem: docs/snowflake-functions.md lists 16 functions as Not checked.
acceptance: Each Not checked row becomes Runs, Differs (difference named) or Refused by name
The summary's Not checked count is 0

WR-319.title: Databricks SQL: the 10 functions that Differ match Databricks or are refused by name
WR-319.problem: docs/databricks-functions.md lists 10 functions as Differs; a different answer that runs is the riskiest kind of gap.
acceptance: Each Differs row is fixed to Runs, or refused by name where the difference can't be closed locally
Tests fail on main without the change

WR-410.title: Audit fail-closed coverage: every write that must be audited first is listed and tested
WR-410.problem: Audit-first rules were added path by path (#3008, #3068); a guard test should list every such path so a new one can't skip it. (Not the earlier capacity WR-410 in publish.py, which reused the number.)
acceptance: A guard test lists every audited-first write path and fails when a new one isn't listed
Each listed path has a test that nothing is written when the audit line can't be written

WR-411.title: Audit trail: Windows Event Log anchor failures say what happened and never block work silently
WR-411.problem: #3088 anchors the audit trail's end in the Windows Application event log; its failure paths need the same care as the trail.
acceptance: An unwritable or missing event source, and a mismatch, each give a named message and an audit-check result
Tests for each failure path

WR-412.title: Privacy: a deletion request leaves a proof of what was deleted, without the data
WR-412.problem: The privacy inventory (#3159) lists the engine's stores; IT needs evidence that a deletion reached each one.
acceptance: Deleting a person's data writes a record of each store touched and the count removed, with no personal values
A test per store in the inventory

WR-413.title: Fuzz the kratosforge:// link and pairing handshake readers
WR-413.problem: These readers take input from outside the app; fuzzing found crashes in other readers (#3176).
acceptance: Seeded fuzz tests for both readers; anything that crashed them is refused by name

WR-414.title: Governance error messages name a next step
WR-414.problem: Governance refusals and failures should read like the rest of the app (#2325).
acceptance: Each governance error string has a next step, checked by a test; UX reviews the copy

WR-130.title: Notebook kernel lifecycle matches Fabric: start, restart, interrupt and idle stop
WR-130.problem: People expect a notebook session to start, restart and stop as in Fabric.
acceptance: Start, restart, interrupt and idle stop behave as Fabric documents or say how they differ
Tests for each, including a restart while a cell runs

WR-132.title: Notebook .ipynb files round-trip without losing cells, outputs or metadata
WR-132.problem: Notebooks move between this PC, Fabric and Git as .ipynb; a lossy round trip loses work. Build on test_notebook_formats_roundtrip.py: check main first and add only what it doesn't cover.
acceptance: An .ipynb from Fabric and from Databricks saves back byte-equal apart from documented fields
What can't be kept is named on save

WR-133.title: Notebook display() and Spark output on this PC look as in Fabric
WR-133.problem: A result that shows differently from Fabric makes people doubt the local run.
acceptance: display() of a DataFrame, show() and a chart output match Fabric's form or the difference is documented
Browser tests for each

WR-134.title: A 2000-cell notebook opens, scrolls, runs and saves within set times
WR-134.problem: Large notebooks are where editors fall over; #2950, #2963 and #3002 test large-notebook saves but not the editor's speed.
acceptance: A 2000-cell notebook opens and saves within a documented bound on the CI runner
Scrolling and run-all stay responsive, measured by counts rather than wall-clock where possible

WR-612.title: Every strict xfail on main names the story that will fix it
WR-612.problem: Nine xfail(strict=True) marks in sidecar/tests pin known wrong answers; without an owner they can stay for good.
acceptance: A guard test fails when a strict xfail's reason doesn't name a story id or issue
Each of today's strict xfails names one

WR-615.title: Tests bound by wall-clock time: count work instead where the time isn't the point
WR-615.problem: About 80 assertions in sidecar/tests bound elapsed time; several flaky failures this week were fixed by counting instead (#3124, #3130, #3148, #3149, #3166).
acceptance: Each wall-clock assertion is either converted to a count or kept with a comment saying why time is the point
The flaky ledger gets a row for any that failed on main in the last 14 days

WR-616.title: Story ids stay unique: a ledger of WR ranges per thread, checked by queues.py
WR-616.problem: This week WR-250 to WR-252 named both SQL translator stories and Prod typed-name fixes, and WR-410 named both a capacity stop and a governance story; reports and handoffs then point at the wrong work.
acceptance: A ledger in docs/product/operations lists each thread's reserved WR range
queues.py check fails when a queued story's id is outside its workstream's ranges or reserved by another thread

WR-135.title: Present mode and the Markdown toolbar hold up on 2,000-cell notebooks and odd Markdown
WR-135.problem: N23 and N49 shipped as Preview with tests on small notebooks and plain Markdown.
acceptance: Slides start at the same headings the Outline reads, underlined ones included, and never inside code, quotes or HTML
Present opens a 2,000-cell notebook within a measured budget, and the toolbar edits a Markdown cell near its end
Toolbar edits on odd selections (spaces at the ends, backticks, fences inside) produce the Markdown they say

WR-136.title: Notebook metadata survives a save: a fuzzed .ipynb round-trip through merge_saved
WR-136.problem: merge_saved keeps the file's own metadata, but the tests use hand-picked notebooks.
acceptance: Generated notebooks with mixed cell, notebook and widget metadata, attachments and slide marks round-trip with only the edit changed
A failure prints the smallest notebook that shows it

WR-137.title: Notebook keyboard shortcuts don't collide across Present, the debugger, the Markdown toolbar and the command bar
WR-137.problem: Present, the debugger and the Markdown toolbar each add keys on the notebook page.
acceptance: A test lists every notebook key and fails on two owners for one key in the same state
Each key does one thing while presenting, debugging or editing Markdown

WR-138.title: Notebook find and replace holds up on regular expressions, Unicode, cell edits and 2,000-cell notebooks
WR-138.problem: Find and replace across cells shipped with tests on a four-cell notebook and plain ASCII text.
acceptance: A regular expression's ^ and $ match at each line, and whole word finds words with accented letters beside emoji
Replace moves on to the next match; the count follows cells deleted while the bar is open
Replace all in a 2,000-cell notebook changes every match, far cells included, and Undo replace all builds no editors
